summary: LLM inference costs are driven primarily by token volume and model tier, with flagship models charging 4-5x more for output than input tokens. By stacking multiple optimization levers—prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, and output constraints—teams routinely achieve 60-80% cost reductions without measurable quality loss. No single technique gets you there; the compound effect of 5-6 stacked strategies is what clears the 70% threshold.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Stores processed input tokens server-side so repeated system prompts, instructions, or large context windows are reused without reprocessing. Most effective for agents and chatbots with large static system prompts across many requests.
techniques.savings: 50-90% on cached input tokens (41-80% total API cost in PwC's 500-session study)
techniques.example: Mark your 10,000-token system prompt as cacheable with Anthropic's cache_control parameter; subsequent calls within the TTL reuse it at a 90% discount on those cached tokens.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches responses keyed by embedding similarity rather than exact string match, so semantically equivalent queries ('reset my password' vs 'how do I change my password') return the cached answer. Requires a similarity threshold to balance hit rate against false matches.
techniques.savings: Up to 73% cost reduction; 45% typical cache hit rate
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed each incoming query, and if cosine similarity to a stored query exceeds 0.95, return the cached response instead of calling the API.

techniques.name: Model Routing (Right-Sizing)
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it—simple classification/extraction to budget models, complex reasoning to flagship models. Often implemented with task-type rules or a lightweight classifier.
techniques.savings: 40-70% reduction (routing was the single biggest lever at $24.50/1,000 in one case study)
techniques.example: Send 70% of traffic to GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash for classification, reserve GPT-4/Opus for the 5% of requests flagged as complex reasoning tasks.

techniques.name: Output Constraints
techniques.description: Caps and structures model output using max_tokens limits and structured output schemas, since output tokens cost 4-5x more than input tokens. Prevents runaway verbose responses that inflate bills.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and request a JSON schema response instead of prose, forcing the model to return only the structured fields you need.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression / Trimming
techniques.description: Reduces input token count by trimming verbose system prompts, removing filler phrases, replacing multiple few-shot examples with a single clear one, and compressing retrieved context. Directly cuts input costs proportionally.
techniques.savings: 30% token reduction (a 30% shorter prompt = 30% lower input cost)
techniques.example: Cut your system prompt from 600 tokens to under 200 by removing redundant instructions and replacing three few-shot examples with one.

techniques.name: Batch Processing
techniques.description: Submits non-urgent requests through provider batch APIs that process asynchronously within 24 hours in exchange for a discount. Ideal for offline jobs like summarization, classification, or evaluation.
techniques.savings: 50% off standard pricing (up to 95% when combined with prompt caching)
techniques.example: Submit your nightly 100,000-document classification job via Anthropic's Batch API to get 50% off, instead of hitting the real-time endpoint.

techniques.name: Multi-Tier Caching
techniques.description: Layers exact-match caching, semantic caching, and session context management so most requests are served from the cheapest available tier before ever reaching the model. Maximizes hit rate while minimizing false matches.
techniques.savings: Substantial compound reduction in token consumption plus latency gains
techniques.example: Check exact-match Redis cache first, fall back to semantic cache on miss, then reuse session context to avoid resending conversation history on every turn.

techniques.name: Quantization & Right-Sizing (Self-Hosted)
techniques.description: For self-hosted inference, quantizing model weights (e.g. INT8/INT4) shrinks memory footprint and lets you run on smaller/cheaper GPUs, while right-sizing matches GPU resource requests to actual peak usage instead of over-provisioning.
techniques.example: Quantize a Llama model to INT4 and deploy on a right-sized GPU so it runs at 70%+ utilization instead of an H100 at 8%.

techniques.name: Continuous Batching & KV Cache Reuse (Runtime)
techniques.description: At the serving-runtime layer, continuous (in-flight) batching, PagedAttention, speculative decoding, and KV cache reuse pack more requests through the same GPU to raise throughput and lower per-request cost.
techniques.example: Serve your model with vLLM to enable continuous batching and PagedAttention, boosting tokens/second per GPU by 40-80% versus naive batching.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching layer for LLM queries that stores responses by embedding similarity, integrates with LangChain and OpenAI, and supports multiple vector stores.

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store offering both exact-match and vector-based semantic caching for LLM responses, with low-latency lookups and TTL control via RedisVL.
tools.pricing_paid: Free self-hosted; Redis Cloud from ~$5/month, enterprise tiers scale up

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK that gives a single OpenAI-compatible interface to 100+ providers, with built-in caching, model routing/fallbacks, rate limiting, and cost tracking.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LiteLLM Enterprise with SSO/support (custom pricing)

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: Observability and gateway platform that logs LLM requests, tracks costs/latency, and provides caching and prompt management via a one-line proxy integration.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/month, enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching (in-memory, SQLite, Redis, GPTCache), prompt templating, and routing primitives for orchestrating optimized pipelines.
tools.pricing_paid: Free open source; LangSmith observability from ~$39/user/month

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine implementing PagedAttention, continuous batching, and prefix/KV cache reuse for efficient self-hosted serving.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source, Apache 2.0); you pay only for your own GPU compute

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: AI gateway providing semantic caching, model routing, automatic fallbacks, load balancing, and cost/latency observability across providers.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier; paid plans from ~$49/month, enterprise custom

tools.name: Cast AI
tools.description: Kubernetes cost-optimization platform that right-sizes GPU requests and automates provisioning to eliminate the over-provisioning that drives self-hosted inference waste.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier/trial; paid plans priced on managed cloud spend

quick_wins: Enable provider prompt caching on your large static system prompts (90% discount on cached tokens, 50-80% total savings) — often a one-parameter change.
Set max_tokens limits and switch to structured JSON output schemas to cut your 4-5x-priced output tokens by roughly 50%.
Trim system prompts to under 200 tokens and replace multiple few-shot examples with one, cutting input cost ~30% immediately.
Add model routing so cheap tasks (classification, extraction) hit GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash and only complex requests reach flagship models (40-70% savings).
Drop in a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) to serve repeat/similar queries from cache, targeting a 40%+ hit rate and up to 73% reduction on those requests.
